title: A Mizoram farmer started growing strawberries in 2024. The UN just named her a global hero. October 28, 2026.
excerpt: From a Mughal emperor whose wife ran half his empire, to a filmmaker's second Venice win in two years, to a one-night gala that raised $214,000 for disabled Indians, to India's best-ever year for wind power, to a strawberry farmer honoured by the UN after just two years in the field - October 28's five stories are about what two years, one night, or one lifetime of quiet persistence can build.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about time working in someone's favor, however short - a four-century-old memoir still read today, a second festival win arriving faster than most careers produce a first, one gala night doubling its own total, one fiscal year breaking a nine-year-old record, and two years turning one farmer into a global name.

October 28, 1627: a Mughal emperor died travelling home from Kashmir - leaving behind an empire run partly by his wife

Emperor Jahangir died in 1627 while travelling back toward Lahore from Kashmir. His wife Nur Jahan wielded major political influence throughout his reign, and his own memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, remains a rare first-person record of Mughal court life.

She won a top Venice Film Festival prize in 2025. In 2026, she won another one - for a different film

Anuparna Roy's "Lovers in the Blue Night" won the NETPAC Award for Best Asian Film at Venice 2026, a year after her debut film won Venice's Orizzonti Best Director award - making her the first Indian filmmaker to win that prize.

A diaspora group's first DC-area gala raised $214,000 for disabled Indians in one night

VOSAP's first Washington D.C. metro-area fundraiser, a sold-out March 2026 gala in Fairfax, Virginia, raised $107,000 from donors - matched dollar-for-dollar by a chief patron couple - funding assistive technology and healthcare access programs for people with disabilities across India.

India just had its best year ever for wind power

India added 6.1 GW of wind capacity in FY26, a 46% jump over the previous year and the highest-ever annual addition on record, beating a record that had stood for nearly a decade.

A Mizoram farmer started growing strawberries in 2024. In 2026, the UN picked her as one of 100 agricultural heroes from 131 countries

ZT Lalrithangi began strawberry farming in her Mizoram village only in 2024. By October 2026, the UN Food and Agriculture Organization honoured her as one of 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems, selected from over 600 candidates worldwide.

Five stories, one pattern: a wife's political influence that outlasted an empire, a director's second win before most careers produce a first, a gala night that doubled itself, a fiscal year that broke a nine-year record, and two years of farming that reached Rome.
